Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement packet we need a short implementation runbook describing how Redwood would meet our Data Processing Framework (DPF) requirements for cross-border processing (EU controller, US processor scenario). Specifically we need:

- Outline of operational steps you take when customers request EU-only residency and the fallback behavior when burst capacity routes to non-EU endpoints.
- How the DPA annex maps to your routing & KV cache controls.
- Expected timeline (detailed milestones) for production onboarding and a minimal evidence bundle we can attach to our privacy assessment.

Can you please provide a short runbook and a draft DPA annex we can review? We are on a tight procurement window — ideally by EOD Tuesday (June 2).

Hi Marta,

Appreciate the clear ask and the timeline. Attached are two artifacts to start: a concise "DPF implementation runbook" and a draft DPA annex showing the clauses we suggest for routing, sub-processing, and evidence attachments. High level answers inline below; the attachments have the detail you can include in your packet.

1) EU-only residency and fallback behavior
- Normal operation: customer selects EU residency; all inference requests route to EU-dedicated pools and remain in EU-hosted runtime.
- Controlled burst: if EU capacity is exceeded, policy options are (a) queue & throttle to preserve residency, (b) overflow to a geo-compatible EU partner pool, or (c) explicit customer-approved fallback to non-EU with token redaction and minimized PII. We default to (a) unless the customer opts into (c) via contract amendment.

2) DPA annex mapping to routing & KV cache controls
- The annex includes: routing policy binding, KV cache scoping (namespace tagging + TTLs), explicit subprocessor list with regions, and audit hooks for per-request routing decisions.
- We include operational controls (network egress filters, KMS key residency metadata) and sample SIEM log fields for per-request location.

3) Onboarding timeline & evidence bundle
- Typical timeline (EU production):
  • Week 0: contract signature + compliance kickoff (info exchange)
  • Weeks 1–2: environment provisioning (EU clusters, KMS keys)
  • Weeks 3–4: routing policy validation, test harness (sample traffic)
  • Week 5: security review & evidence handoff (SOC 2 summary, audit logs extract, DPA annex)
  • Week 6: go-live (can be accelerated with an SLA for provisioning)

- Minimal evidence bundle: signed DPA annex, isolation proof (routing config snapshot), KMS key manifest, sample audit-log export (anonymized), SOC 2 report summary.

Attachments included: redwood-dpf-runbook.pdf (overview + procedural checklist) and dpa-annex-draft.docx (track-changes friendly).

I cc'd Marissa (privacy lead) and Karthik (legal/integration) to review anything you want tightened. If you need a short recorded walkthrough we can arrange 30–45 minutes tomorrow.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Trust | Redwood Inference
